name: POST /api/api-keys - Issue an API key
description: Issues a key without naming the application in the path; application_id may still travel in the body. The tenant comes from the caller claims - it used to be read from the payload with no ownership check at all, which let any signed-in user mint and manage credentials against any tenant on the platform. A payload tenant_id that disagrees with the credential is now a 403 rather than being silently ignored, because ignoring it hides a misconfigured caller until it writes somewhere it should not. Plaintext is returned exactly once. Every key is bound to a MACHINE-KIND PERSONA created in the SAME transaction as the key (TK-4138): synthetic_persona_id in the response resolves to a real persona.persona row, and api_keys.key.synthetic_persona_id now carries an FK to it, so a key referencing a missing persona is unrepresentable rather than failing much later as a 23503 during a role grant. One machine person/app_identity/membership is shared per (tenant, application) and ONE persona is minted per key, so audit and ReBAC can tell one credential from another. Rotation deliberately REUSES the predecessor's persona - a rotated key is the same machine identity with new material.

testCases.name: Issue a key naming the application in the body

errorCases.name: A payload naming a different tenant is refused
